% SCI-BEAM v0.1 shared normative equations. Document revision r0.3.
\section{Normative scientific model}
\label{sec:equations}

\subsection{Raw signal, coordinate metric, and map-domain fit}

For detector $d$, the raw uncalibrated observable and detector collection are
\begin{equation}
x_d(t)\equiv\frac{\Delta f_d(t)}{f_d},
\qquad \mathbf x(t)=\{x_d(t)\}_d .
\label{eq:raw-signal}
\end{equation}
The standardized detector Beammap $x^{\rm BM}_{d,p}$ remains in $\Delta f/f$.
Its physical fit coordinate is
\begin{equation}
\boldsymbol\vartheta_p=f_{\rm WCS}(r_p,c_p),
\qquad
\mathbf J_{{\rm sky},p}=
\left.\frac{\partial(\vartheta_x,\vartheta_y)}{\partial(r,c)}\right|_{(r_p,c_p)} .
\label{eq:wcs}
\end{equation}
The full transformation shall be evaluated per pixel unless a declared local
linearization has bounded error over the complete fit region.

Let
\begin{align}
\mathbf R(\theta)&=
\begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\ \sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{bmatrix},\\
\boldsymbol\Sigma_{\rm eff}&=
\mathbf R(\theta)\,
\mathrm{diag}(\sigma_{\rm maj}^2,\sigma_{\rm min}^2)\,
\mathbf R(\theta)^\mathsf T,\\
G(\mathbf u;\boldsymbol\Sigma_{\rm eff})&=
\exp\!\left(-\tfrac12\mathbf u^\mathsf T
\boldsymbol\Sigma_{\rm eff}^{-1}\mathbf u\right),\\
H(\mathbf u;\boldsymbol\Sigma_{\rm eff},\boldsymbol\phi)&=
\int S(\mathbf t;\boldsymbol\phi)
G(\mathbf u-\mathbf t;\boldsymbol\Sigma_{\rm eff})\,d^2\mathbf t,\\
T(\mathbf u;\boldsymbol\Sigma_{\rm eff},\boldsymbol\phi)&=
\frac{H(\mathbf u;\boldsymbol\Sigma_{\rm eff},\boldsymbol\phi)}
{H(\mathbf0;\boldsymbol\Sigma_{\rm eff},\boldsymbol\phi)} .
\label{eq:template}
\end{align}
The admitted source model shall satisfy
\begin{equation}
S\ge0,\qquad
\int S(\mathbf u;\boldsymbol\phi)d^2\mathbf u=1,\qquad
\int\mathbf uS(\mathbf u;\boldsymbol\phi)d^2\mathbf u=\mathbf0,
\qquad H(\mathbf0)>0.
\label{eq:source}
\end{equation}
Thus $T(\mathbf0)=1$ at the declared reference origin, which need not be the
global maximum for an asymmetric source.

The canonical v0.1 map-domain model is
\begin{equation}
x^{\rm BM}_{d,p}=
A_d^{\rm obs}
T\!\left(\boldsymbol\vartheta_p-\boldsymbol\mu_{d,\rm fit};
\boldsymbol\Sigma_{{\rm eff},d},\boldsymbol\phi\right)
+\mathbf b_p^\mathsf T\boldsymbol\beta_d+r_{d,p} .
\label{eq:model}
\end{equation}
The effective tensor summarizes the core already embodied in the standardized
map response. Equation~\ref{eq:model} is not a deconvolution of mapmaking,
pixelization, filtering, finite support, or any other parent response.

For admitted map covariance, the estimator minimizes
\begin{equation}
Q_d=(\mathbf x_d^{\rm BM}-\mathbf m_d)^\mathsf T
(\mathbf C_d^{\rm BM})^{-1}(\mathbf x_d^{\rm BM}-\mathbf m_d)
+\log|\mathbf C_d^{\rm BM}|,
\label{eq:objective}
\end{equation}
up to additive constants. A declared approximation
$\widetilde{\mathbf C}_d^{\rm BM}$ may replace $\mathbf C_d^{\rm BM}$ only
with conditional labels. Singular covariance requires a declared retained-
subspace or regularization procedure; silent replacement is forbidden.

\subsection{Model Jacobian, covariance, and derived shape}

For every realized free parameter $q_j$, including amplitude, centroid, all
three independent tensor degrees of freedom, background, and admitted source
nuisance parameters, the fit resolves
\begin{equation}
J^{\rm fit}_{ij}=\frac{\partial m_i}{\partial q_j}.
\label{eq:model-jacobian}
\end{equation}
Analytic, automatic, or verified numerical differentiation may realize the
Jacobian. A local likelihood covariance may be reported as
\begin{equation}
\mathbf V_{q,d}=\left[
\tfrac12\nabla\nabla^\mathsf TQ_d(\widehat{\mathbf q}_d)
\right]^{-1}
\label{eq:fitcov}
\end{equation}
only for an identifiable interior solution under the declared likelihood and
covariance model. The map-fit covariance retains material
width--orientation, centroid--shape, amplitude--width,
background--centroid, source--beam, and coordinate--shape terms among the
fitted and admitted map-model parameters.

For calibration and sensitivity, let $\boldsymbol\eta_d$ contain the external
calibrator source flux, nominal-beam convention, source atmosphere,
source-model systematic terms, scan-noise statistic, exposure normalization,
and other admitted derived-stage inputs. A separate derived-product Jacobian
$\mathbf J^{\rm drv}_{(q,\eta)}$ propagates the joint fit/input covariance:
\begin{equation}
\mathbf V_{{\rm drv},d}=\mathbf J^{\rm drv}_{(q,\eta)}
\mathbf V_{(q,\eta)}
\left(\mathbf J^{\rm drv}_{(q,\eta)}\right)^\mathsf T .
\label{eq:nuisance}
\end{equation}
Material dependence between fit and derived stages is retained.
Omitted material terms are named and prohibit a ``total'' label. At
circularity shape covariance is expressed in an invariant tensor basis and
angle uncertainty is unavailable.

The compact Gaussian-core quantities are
\begin{equation}
{\rm FWHM}_{\rm maj,min}=2\sqrt{2\ln2}\,\sigma_{\rm maj,min},
\qquad
\Omega_G=2\pi\sigma_{\rm maj}\sigma_{\rm min}.
\label{eq:fwhm-area}
\end{equation}
$\Omega_G$ is available only as the fitted Gaussian-core solid angle under a
declared interpretation; it is not automatically the complete beam solid
angle.

For compatible nominal/effective Gaussian and response conventions,
\begin{equation}
\boldsymbol\Sigma_{{\rm broad},d}=
\boldsymbol\Sigma_{{\rm eff},d}-\boldsymbol\Sigma_{{\rm nom},a(d)} .
\label{eq:broadening}
\end{equation}
A literal Gaussian-broadening interpretation requires the difference to be
positive semidefinite within propagated uncertainty. Otherwise the tensor is
unavailable as a smoothing kernel and the indefinite result remains
model-inadequacy or convention-incompatibility evidence.

\subsection{Relative coordinates, derotation, and pivot status}

Let $\mathbf r_{od}$ denote the fitted relative coordinate in the
observation-local plane and $\mathbf u_d$ the horizon-fixed relative
coordinate. The exact fitted-centroid relation is
\begin{equation}
\mathbf r_{od}=
\mathbf S_{\mu\rightarrow x,o}\boldsymbol\mu_{d,\rm fit},
\label{eq:centroid-to-detector}
\end{equation}
where the declared transformation supplies the source-centroid to
detector-coordinate sign and frame convention. It shall not be inferred from
implementation behavior. The physical rotation relation is affine,
\begin{equation}
\mathbf r_{od}=
\mathbf R(\chi_{od})\mathbf u_d+\mathbf t_o(\chi_{od}),
\label{eq:affine-rotation}
\end{equation}
where the common translation contains the arbitrary coordinate-origin gauge
and any unresolved pivot/pointing term. The v0.1 derotated product uses the
declared conventional transform
\begin{equation}
\mathbf u_d=
\mathbf R(-\chi_{d,\rm eff})
\left(\mathbf r_{od}-\mathbf o_{\rm conv}\right),
\qquad
\boldsymbol\Sigma_{d,\rm hor}=
\mathbf R(-\chi_{d,\rm eff})\boldsymbol\Sigma_{d,\rm raw}
\mathbf R(-\chi_{d,\rm eff})^\mathsf T,
\label{eq:derotation}
\end{equation}
with deterministic common recentering. $\mathbf o_{\rm conv}$ is not a
physical boresight unless separately established. $\chi_{d,\rm eff}$ is
derived from the parent-sample time/elevation support and contribution weights
$w^{\rm BM}_{d,p,t}$ that formed pixels $p\in\mathcal I_d$, propagated through
the realized pixel-domain fit support. Pixel fit weights alone do not resolve
parent timing. A single observation-average angle is allowed only with
negligible validated error.

\subsection{Top-of-atmosphere calibration and sensitivity}

The source model supplies $F^{\rm TOA,nom}_{s,a}$ in
$\mathrm{mJy\,beam_{nom}^{-1}}$ for the fixed nominal beam at the same
reference origin as $A_d^{\rm obs}$. With source-observation correction
$C^{\rm eff}_{s,a}=1/T^{\rm eff}_{s,a}$,
\begin{align}
A_d^{\rm TOA-eq}&=C^{\rm eff}_{s,a}A_d^{\rm obs},\\
\mathrm{flxscale}_d&=
\frac{F^{\rm TOA,nom}_{s,a}}{A_d^{\rm TOA-eq}}
=\frac{T^{\rm eff}_{s,a}F^{\rm TOA,nom}_{s,a}}{A_d^{\rm obs}} .
\label{eq:flxscale}
\end{align}
The factor has role and unit
$[\mathrm{mJy\,beam_{nom}^{-1}}/(\Delta f/f)]_{\rm TOA}$.
Its uncertainty is obtained from the separate derived-product Jacobian in
Equation~\ref{eq:nuisance}, using the joint covariance of the map-fit amplitude
and the nominal source flux, atmosphere, and other material derived-stage inputs.
Source atmosphere appears here; target atmosphere remains outside SCI-BEAM.

For detector-specific off-source scan set $\mathcal S_{d,\rm off}$,
\begin{align}
n_{d,s}^{\rm obs}&=\mathcal N[x_{d,s}(t)],\\
n_{d,s}^{\rm TOA-eq}&=C^{\rm eff}_{s,a,s}\,n_{d,s}^{\rm obs},\\
n_d^{\rm off}&=\operatorname{median}_{s\in\mathcal S_{d,\rm off}}
n_{d,s}^{\rm TOA-eq},\\
\mathrm{sens}_d&=|\mathrm{flxscale}_d|\,n_d^{\rm off}.
\label{eq:sens}
\end{align}
$\mathcal N$ includes a declared time/exposure normalization so
$n_d^{\rm off}$ has $\Delta f/f\sqrt{\rm s}$ and \texttt{sens} has
$\mathrm{mJy\,beam_{nom}^{-1}\sqrt{s}}$. An available \texttt{sens} is finite
and strictly positive. The physical sign of \texttt{flxscale} is retained in
the calibration record and only its magnitude enters Equation~\ref{eq:sens}.
The exact source exclusion,
scan admission, baseline, frequency/bandwidth, robust statistic, correlated-
noise, minimum-count, exposure, partial-scan, and uncertainty rules remain
owner-controlled. The retained scan scatter is a required stability or
uncertainty diagnostic. Approximate downstream weights may satisfy
$\omega_d\propto\mathrm{sens}_d^{-2}$ only under a separately governed
weighting policy.

\subsection{Observation-local convergence}

An observation-local iteration may alternate locator and measurement phases.
The effective policy declares per-parameter metrics $d_j$ and scales $s_j$,
objective scale $s_Q$, tolerances, support and valid-detector stability rules,
a consecutive-transition count, and $N_{\max}$. Orientation uses
\[
d_\pi(a,b)=\min_{n\in\mathbb Z}|a-b+n\pi|.
\]
With parameter-availability set $\mathcal A_d^{(k)}$, selected candidate
$c_d^{(k)}$, support $\mathcal I_d^{(k)}$, and valid-detector set
$\mathcal V^{(k)}$, convergence requires
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\max_{j\in\mathcal A_d^{(k)}\cap\mathcal A_d^{(k-1)}}
\frac{d_j(q_j^{(k)},q_j^{(k-1)})}{s_j}&\le\epsilon_j,
&\mathcal A_d^{(k)}&=\mathcal A_d^{(k-1)},\\
\frac{|Q^{(k)}-Q^{(k-1)}|}{s_Q}&\le\epsilon_Q,
&c_d^{(k)}&=c_d^{(k-1)},\\
\mathcal I_d^{(k)}&=\mathcal I_d^{(k-1)},
&\mathcal V^{(k)}&=\mathcal V^{(k-1)}.
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:convergence}
\end{equation}
for the declared number of consecutive transitions. Availability changes fail
stability; a parameter unavailable at both transitions contributes no numeric
metric. Optimizer completion alone is never scientific convergence, and v0.1
defines no universal numeric defaults.
